set.approach: The slab is reached from a pullout on the westbound Trans-Canada Highway, roughly midway between the Mount Norquay turnoff and the Bow Valley Parkway turnoff. Cross the animal fence at the runoff channel and follow the channel a short way, then climb the ridge on its right under the power lines and through burned timber, picking up a faint trail to the crest. Follow the crest past flat spots and rock steps; where the ridge dips to a col and then steepens, take the trail round to the right and onto the ridge again. A slab blocks the ridge at the next flat spot, so drop down and left past a cairn, cross a stand of trees and a wide scree-filled gully, staying left of it (ignore the trail that heads up to a rock step). Follow the downhill trail to the edge of a cliff, which is the top of the lower slab, turn right along it to an opening, and the upper slab lies straight ahead. The route climbs the corner immediately to the right of Escargot Corner.

review.notes: Approach from the Upper Norquay Slab area page; start from the route text (corner right of Escargot). No descent stated for this route or the slab page.

set.descent_text: From the top-out ledge walk up and left, then up and right onto the ridge system. Follow the ridge down to a sharp drop, where a boulder wrapped in a black chain serves as the rappel anchor. Rappel to easier ground, then scramble down the ridge to rejoin the approach trail.

review.notes: Approach from the area page; start and descent from the route page (one source for the descent).

set.approach: Park at the roadside on the Icefields Parkway a few hundred metres south of the Weeping Wall, beside a collection of large boulders. Vacation Wall is the main multi-pitch wall behind the boulder: continue up past the boulder to reach it. The route climbs the rock directly behind the line called El Penata Clamor.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route from its bolted belays.

review.notes: Approach from Weeping Wall Rock and Vacation Wall pages, start from route Location; rappel stated on the route page only.

set.approach: South of Jasper, take the Icefields Parkway side road (Highway 93A) past Athabasca Falls to Leech Lake and park at the pullout. A maintained trail leads into the forest to the Lost Boys crag. Wasted Youth Wall is the sector right of the Main Wall. Bloodline follows the obvious big flake with a wide crack at the right end of the Main Wall, marked at its base with painted letters and a number in yellow.

review.notes: Approach from Lost Boys and wall pages; start from route Location. Only rap hangers are mentioned for the anchors, so no descent written.
